Backfill progress (D14) and cost (R1-D4): also the shape of
[`Endless::backfill_estimate`] before a backfill starts.

done.description: History units with a level-0 line.

eta_secs.description: Remaining × measured seconds per unit (5 s before any node is built).

total.description: History units to cover (after the `backfill_max_units` cap).

usd_estimate.description: Remaining × measured USD per unit ($0.02 before any node is built).

event.agent_2eendless_2dprogress.output..description:
Unsummarized lines waiting for the compactor (137G). Engine → UI. TS name
`EndlessBacklog`: `dreaming::Backlog` owns `Backlog.ts`.

eta_secs.description: Estimate at the measured throughput; 0 when paused or unknown.

folded.description: Of those, how many the view currently shows folded into one placeholder line (the raw budget).

paused.description: Settling is paused for this session (no compactor calls).

paused_by.description: Who paused: `"user"` (`endless_pause`) or `"spend"` (the G11 day cap); `None` while running.

event.agent_2eendless_2dprogress.output..description: Bus event on the session stream, ≤ 1 per 500 ms per session (§11.2).

backfill.description: D14 progress while history is being covered.

error.description: First failure of a node (reported once per node).

settling.description: Some view part is still being built.

stalled.description: 137F: as [`SessionMemory::stalled`]; emitted whenever it appears, its count changes or it clears.

event.agent_2eendless_2dprogress.output..description: Identifies a conversation; every event carries one.

blocking.description: The failing node is the level-0 frontier: newer lines wait behind it.

error.description: The last error, one line, ≤ 300 chars (secrets never appear: it is the provider's message).

failures.description: Consecutive failed attempts of the failing node that blocks most (the frontier first).

model.description: The compactor model id that failed.

next_retry_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time of the pump's own next retry; `None` while a retry is running.

event.agent_2eevents.output.AdvisorConsu.description: `consult` calls answered for one link (125 R1 D-R1.7).

total.description: Consults answered for this link since it was created: the root's and its subagents'.

turn.description: Consults in the advised session's current user turn (its own; subagents not folded in).

event.agent_2eevents.output.AdvisorNoteC.description: Notes emitted so far, by severity.

event.agent_2eevents.output.AdvisorSever.description:
Severity of one advisor note (125 §4.8); ordered so a card's severity is
the max of its notes.

oneOf.description:
The answer to a consultation (125 R1); never emitted by `advise`,
never steered, never posted. First: it ranks below `Nit`, so a
worst-of pick never promotes a card to `Advice`.
Batched into one card at the next step boundary.
Steered into the running turn; preserved as a card after a terminal answer.
Steered; opens a turn when the session is idle.

event.agent_2eevents.output.AdvisorState.description: Live state of one advisor link (125 §4.3).

oneOf.description: Linked, waiting for the next step.
The advisor session is running a review turn.
Paused on a usage limit; the batch is retained.
Halted after repeated failures or a permanent rejection.

event.agent_2eevents.output.AdvisorStatu.description:
Everything a UI shows about one session's advisor (125 §6.2): the pill,
the popover and `/advisor status`. `state: Off` with everything else
default when the session has none.

backlog.description: Deltas waiting while the advisor is busy (125 §4.6).

context_used.description: Tokens of the advisor's context in use.

detail.description: Why paused/halted, first line.

effort.description: Effort of the advisor.

model.description: `provider/model` of the advisor.

tokens_in.description: Prompt tokens spent by the advisor.

tokens_out.description: Completion tokens spent by the advisor.

warning.description:
D-R1.5 pairing warning, set once at attach/re-pick when the advisor's
catalog output price is below the advised session's model's; `None`
when either price is unknown or the order is fine.

event.agent_2eevents.output.Advisory.description:
One Advisory card: every note the advisor emitted for one step boundary
(nits batched), one steer (125 §6.2), or one consultation's answer (R1).

oneOf.description: The watchdog's notes (every row written before R1).
The answer to a `consult` call; `notes` holds exactly one `Advice` note.

advisor.description: The advisor session (never shown to the model).

at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the card was raised.

notes.description: At least one; the card's severity is the max.

step.description: `AdvisorStep` count of the link when the notes were raised.

turn.description: Opener seq of the advised turn under review; `None` when idle.

note.description: The note text, normalised by the emission guard.

event.agent_2eevents.output.AgentEvent.description:
Everything a UI needs to render a session live. Every variant carries the
session and turn; UIs filter by session.

oneOf.description: A user message was accepted and a model request is starting.

channel.description: 172: the channel that delivered the opening user text, if any.

model.description: Canonical model id the turn runs on.

text.description: The user text (echo for UIs that did not send it).

turn_seq.description: Seq of the stored user row that opened the turn (design doc 29 §4.2).

oneOf.description: Streamed reasoning text (providers that expose it).

The thinking that `ReasoningDelta` streamed has ended (91): `ms` from
the first reasoning chunk to the first non-reasoning event of the same
model call. Published before the text/tool chunk that ended it.

The model has begun emitting a tool call (name known, arguments still
streaming). Lets a UI show activity before `ToolCallStarted`.

Tool arguments still streaming: the cumulative partial JSON so far
(genai delivers cumulative strings, 00 §11.4). Coalesced: at most one
per 250 ms per call and only after ≥ 512 new bytes. Not persisted; UIs
may jsonrepair it to name what is being written (design doc 35 §3.6).

args.description: Cumulative argument JSON so far (may be truncated mid-token).

oneOf.description: The model asked for a tool; the call is now routed to the registry.

args.description: Raw arguments; UIs format these per tool.

files.description: Files the tool produced (screenshots, generated images); absolute paths on this machine.

output.description: Output text, possibly truncated for display.

oneOf.description: The turn ended (model finished, was cancelled, or errored).

context.description: Prompt + completion tokens of the last model call: what the window holds now.

usage.description: Token usage summed over the turn's model calls.

oneOf.description: Non-fatal or fatal error text for the UI.

turn.description: Turn, if one was in flight.

oneOf.description:
A [`Steer`] is waiting for the current tool batch to end (or, with
`defer`, for the turn to end; 62 §0.3).

channel.description: 172: the channel that delivered this steer, if any.

defer.description: `true`: lands at the next turn, not after this tool batch.

oneOf.description:
A queued input entered the context as a user message; published before
`TurnStarted` when queued inputs start a turn.
A queued input was pulled back by [`Withdraw`]; it never entered the context.
145 §0.3: harness inputs parked behind a closed spoken window.
A subagent session was created for `parent`.

agent.description: External harness (`agents.yaml` key) the child runs on; `None` = theuth.

cap.description: `spawn_subagent(tools=…)` ceiling for the child and its descendants; `None` = no cap.

model.description:
The child's model as [`AgentInfo::model`] at spawn; `None` while
unknown (a harness that has not reported one and no model asked).

name.description: Peer name, unique among the parent's children.

parent.description: Owning session.

oneOf.description:
A watch-only child of `parent` was created or changed (141 §7.5): an
upsert, also on every state/detail change (detail-only changes are
throttled ≥ 250 ms per child). Not [`Self::SubagentSpawned`]: nothing
here is drivable, so channels bind no thread/topic to it.

model.description: The child's own model when the source reports one.

observed.description: Source, external id, state, cost rule, detail.

parent.description: The ACP child (or the observed parent when nested).

oneOf.description:
Text injected into `session` by the harness (subagent result, peer
message, finished or quiet job), for transcripts.

contact.description:
216 §7.3: the sender is a contact (186, `PeerOrigin.contact_mode` set); external
plugins then see no `text`. `false` for children, parent, jobs and the owner.

from.description:
Sender: a child's name, `"parent"`, or `"job j3"` for a
`<job_result>` or a `<job_idle>` (61).

oneOf.description: The session's model was switched (takes effect on its next model call).

model.description: Canonical model id.

oneOf.description:
The default model for new sessions changed (82 §3): a manual
[`SetModel`] made `model` the new `agent.model`. Global, no session.

model.description: Canonical model id.

oneOf.description:
The favorite model list changed (127 §1): a [`SetModelFavorite`]
starred or unstarred a model. Global, no session; `models` is the
whole new list in favorites order.

models.description: Canonical model ids, in the order they were starred.

oneOf.description:
An external harness (ACP child, design doc 06 §8.2) reported the LLM
model its session runs on — at connect, or when it switched
mid-session. `TurnStarted.model` stays the harness name.

model.description: The harness's model id (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`).

oneOf.description:
An external harness announced its command manifest
(`available_commands_update`, design doc 75 §3): loaded skills
(`skill:<name>` on omp) and slash commands. Published only on change.

commands.description: The full manifest, replacing the previous one.

oneOf.description: The session's reasoning effort was set or cleared (takes effect on its next turn).

effort.description: Effort keyword or budget; `None` = provider default.

oneOf.description:
The default effort for new sessions changed (83 §3): a manual
[`SetEffort`] made `effort` the new `agent.effort`. Global, no session.

effort.description: Effort keyword or budget; `None` = provider default.

oneOf.description: Compaction started: the summariser call is in flight (design doc 07 §8).
Compaction finished: a new epoch opened.

after.description:
Estimated tokens of the whole next request (system, tools, head,
kept tail), scaled by the session's calibration: what the gauge
shows as `≈` until the provider's next usage (70 COMPACT-SIZE).

style.description: Style actually used (cut if the summariser fell back).

oneOf.description: A harvest finished for a session (design doc 10 §5.4).

The set of skills whose body is in the frame changed (design doc 04
§2.4): a user injection, a `load_skill` call, or a compaction that
dropped them all.

skills.description: Skill names, sorted; empty right after a compaction.

oneOf.description:
The session's title was set: first words of the first input, the
titler's rewrite (07 §15), or [`RenameSession`].

tags.description:
Tags in force after this change: the titler's set, or the
unchanged stored set on a rename or placeholder.

oneOf.description:
"What's next?": up to three next steps the user might send after `turn`
ended normally, from the title model ([`suggest`]). Ephemeral UI state for
the latest turn only: never a transcript row, never persisted; a turn that
started since makes it stale (it is then not published). Interactive
root chats only, while `agent.suggestions` is on.

items.description: Suggestions, each as the user would type it; never empty.

turn.description: The finished turn the suggestions follow.

oneOf.description: The session's rows are gone ([`DeleteSession`]); lists drop it.

Ownership moved (68 §4.2): `owner` now holds the live actor and
writes the transcript; `here` says whether that is this engine.

moved_from.description:
181 D4: the taker's event for a move (`TakeReason::Moved`): the
engine that sent the session here. `None` for every other change.

oneOf.description:
The session's effective context changed outside a normal turn
(design doc 48 §3.2): a [`RemoveContext`] commit, a settled turn /
compaction handback, or an undo/redo. Published after commit and
installation in live state; carries no bodies. Clients reload the
affected session's history at `revision`.

reason.description:
`"context_edit"`, `"settled"`, `"rewind"`, `"trim"` or `"cell_nudge"` (220: a
plain fence of a finished reply was rewritten as a user cell in place).

oneOf.description:
The session's canonical plan changed (47 §5.1): a native `todo`
mutation committed with its tool result, an ACP plan update, a clear,
or a rewind selecting another list. Full snapshots replace earlier
state; apply only a higher `version`. No turn: a rewind changes the
plan between turns.

snapshot.description: The whole list with its projection version.

oneOf.description:
A vision consultation step (design doc 52 §5.1): `Questioning` when
the main model is asked to write the question (`model` = main id),
`Inspecting` when the fallback call starts (`model` = fallback id),
`Completed` / `Failed` once the note row committed, with its `seq`.
`sources` are the images of this consultation, original coordinates.

model.description: Canonical id of the model this step calls (or called).

seq.description: Seq of the committed note row; `Some` only for `Completed` / `Failed`.

oneOf.description:
The agent's own one-line status (design 212 §9); replaces the generic activity word
in clients until the turn ends.

status.description: What the agent says it is doing now (≤ 80 chars).

title.description: The new title, when this call retitled the session.

oneOf.description:
The root's metadata changed (51 §3): `project` is the new effective
value for the whole tree. Published after the commit.

project.description: New project label; `None` = ungrouped.

oneOf.description:
The accounting ledger of `session` changed (design doc 51 §6.4);
re-read `session_cost` when `revision` is newer than what is shown.

session.description: Owner whose revision moved (the mutated owner or a live ancestor).

oneOf.description:
The window gauge moved mid-turn: one model round of `turn` settled and
`context` is what `TurnFinished.context` will report if no round follows
(prompt + completion of that round). Published on the same cadence as
`ModelUsageChanged` so the context meter moves with the cost (51 §6.4).

context.description: Prompt + completion tokens of the round that just settled.

size.description:
Context window size when the source knows it: an external
harness's `usage_update.size` (75 §5). Native rounds pass `None`
and clients fall back to the model catalog.

oneOf.description:
A private root tree is closing (51 §4.4): every member's data is
being torn down under `generation`; owners fence late writes on it.
`SessionDeleted` follows per member once cleanup ends.

generation.description:
Lifecycle generation being torn down; writers holding an older
one must drop their work.

oneOf.description:
109 §8.2: an open turn is being resumed after a restart (crash) or a
drain (`Suspended`); published before anything else happens.

139 §6.3 (D5): a system-initiated takeover found an open turn and did
**not** resume it; the Attention actor raises `resume:<s>:<t>` with
the takeover detail and the user presses Resume (`resume_turn`).
Published by W2's `Take::run` step 9′; consumed by W1's attention.

from.description: The engine the session was taken from.

oneOf.description: 109 §8.2: the resumed batch was reassembled; the banner's counts.

children_handed_off.description: ACP children replaced by a fresh child with a handoff (§7.3).

interrupted.description: `(call_id, name)` of rows marked `interrupted`: effect unknown.

lost_jobs.description: Jobs that died with the engine (§5).

replayed.description: `(call_id, name)` of calls run as a new attempt.

oneOf.description: 109 §9: a drain could not finish the turn; a `suspended` step was written.

109 §8.2: the streamed partial of the open model call was discarded;
the re-issued call regenerates it.

call_id.description: The model call whose `assistant_partial` was dropped.

oneOf.description: 125 §6.2: the advisor of `session` changed state, model, counters or cost.

125 §6.2: an Advisory row was appended to `session` (steer or aside);
`seq` is its row.

seq.description: Seq of the stored user row carrying the advisory.

oneOf.description:
199: a contact file changed state, or moved bytes (at most twice a second per
file). Cards key it by `(file.holder, file.id)`.

session.description: The chat the file belongs to.

oneOf.description:
`session`'s own knowledge harvester changed (`set_session_knowledge_harvester`);
`harvester.model: None` = back on the default.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ChannelChat.description: 172: a direct conversation or a shared one.

oneOf.description: A Slack channel; a Telegram group, supergroup or forum topic.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ChannelOrigi.description: 172: which channel delivered a user row (UIs show it as a chip; the model input is unchanged).

chat.description: dm | group — a Slack channel and a Telegram group, supergroup or forum topic are `group`; Signal is DM-only today.

from.description: The sender's label when it is not the owner (an allowed user), as the channel already names them.

title.description: The channel or group title when the channel knows it (Slack channel name without `#`, Telegram group title).

oneOf.description: Telegram (private chat, group, supergroup or forum topic).
216 §10.3: a plugin's `input` request; `ChannelOrigin.from` is the plugin name, `chat` is `dm`.

event.agent_2eevents.output.CompactStyle.description: How a compaction builds the new epoch head (design doc 11).

oneOf.description: Drop the folded span, keep the tail, no model call.
Rasterize the folded span to images. Named in v0; not built.

`/clear` (11 §2.4): fold everything, keep nothing, no model call. Manual only —
never a default or automatic style.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ContactFile.description:
One file between contacts as a card shows it (`ContactFileChanged`,
`PeerDelivered.files`, `contact_file`). Keys: `(holder, id)`.

blake3.description: Declared or computed BLAKE3, 64 lowercase hex.

contact_id.description: `ContactFacts.id`, the contact's record id; never the alias.

holder.description: The holder's endpoint id: the engine that stores (in) or serves (out) the bytes.

id.description: The holder's local id, 32 lowercase hex.

path.description: In: the saved path on the holder.

size.description: Declared, then actual size; `None` only for a P3 download in flight.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ContextOwner.description: Which stored row a binary occurrence lives in.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ContextTarge.description:
A removable occurrence, addressed by stored coordinates (48 §3.1). `part`
and `image` index the **original** arrays, never the filtered ones.

oneOf.description: One binary part, or one image inside a tool response part.

image.description: `Some`: index into the `ToolResponse.images` of that part.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts.

oneOf.description: One surface fence inside one text part of an assistant row (197 §3).

index.description: 0-based ordinal of the surface fences of that original text part ([`surface_fences`]).

owner.description: The row; only `Message` owners have fences.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts (a text part).

oneOf.description: The source argument of one `show` / `app` / `page_preview` call part (197 §3).

owner.description: The row; only `Message` owners have sources.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts (a tool call part).

event.agent_2eevents.output.CostBucket.description:
Aggregated spend (§6.2). Monetary partition per call: returned bucket when
a returned value exists, else the estimate bucket, else `unavailable`.

calls.description: Attempts that were reserved and not conclusively `not_dispatched`.

estimated_for_unavailable.description: Adapter estimates for calls without a returned value, per currency, sorted.

returned.description: Provider-reported (and remote-meter attributed) money, one entry per currency, sorted.

unavailable.description: Settled attempts with no money observation (overflowed sums included).

unresolved.description: Attempts left open by a crash; outcome unknown.

event.agent_2eevents.output.CostRule.description:
How a watch-only child's cost relates to its parent's (141 §7.6, D8).
Chosen by the adapter that sees the frame; stored by the agent crate.

oneOf.description:
The child's cost is its own meter rows and rolls up (omp background
spawns: excluded from the harness's `usage_update`).
Already inside the parent's meter; display-only (omp sync spawns).
Reported by the harness, not aggregated (RFD `idle.usage`).

event.agent_2eevents.output.HarnessComma.description:
One entry of an external harness's command manifest
(`available_commands_update`, design doc 75 §3). omp announces loaded
skills as `skill:<name>` and extension commands as `/ponytail…`;
opencode strips the source, so skills and commands are indistinguishable.

hint.description: `input.hint`: what the command takes after its name, when it takes input.

event.agent_2eevents.output.InState.description: An incoming file's state; `Received` and `Failed` are terminal.

oneOf.description: Verified; being linked into place (resolved by inode on restart).
Published while its exchange is still `accepted` or `held`: waits for it.
Published, and its notice durably queued.

event.agent_2eevents.output.InputId.description:
One user input, identified by its sender so it can be shown before any
reply arrives.

event.agent_2eevents.output.Money.description:
A nonnegative amount of one ISO 4217 currency, in integer nanos of the
unit. Never converted between currencies.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, three ASCII uppercase letters (`USD`).

nanos.description: Integer nanos of one currency unit; a decimal string over JSON.

event.agent_2eevents.output.ObservedMeta.description:
Watch-only facts of an `observed` row (141 §5.1), carried on
[`AgentInfo`], [`SessionSummary`], [`Loaded`] and
[`AgentEvent::ObservedChildChanged`].

can_cancel.description: The harness accepts `session/cancel` for this child (RFD `capabilities.cancel`).

detail.description:
Source-specific live fields (`observed_detail`, 141 §6 mapping tables);
`null` when none were stored.

external.description: The harness's own id for the child (`sessions.acp_session`).

message arrives like a mesh peer's, the receiving agent replies with
`send_message(reply_to)` any number of times and the chat's own tool policy applies.
`Cautious` (183's one capped turn per message, the reply the turn text) is only read: from
old rows and an older contact's card (absent = cautious).

oneOf.description: A knowledge concept; the derived file is `knowledge/<id>.md` and the first block is the frontmatter.
An agent's charter — the body of `agents/<name>.md` (67 §6.1); the roster copies each export into the file.

A task's thread (67 §7.1): comments, answers and the event log of one task. Owned by the task,
so it never lists as a note.

A board (71 §2.1): a note the agent draws for a reader — sections, anchored prose, `Excerpt`s and
diagrams — bound like a note (`Binding::Note`, `documents/<id>/note.md`); its first block is the
frontmatter carrying `root:`, the absolute repository root every `code:` link and `ref` resolves against.

A notebook (144 §3.1): the container over notes, sources, sessions and artifacts. Its body is the
description the agent reads as a prompt block; its lists are `notebook_items` rows. Never lists
among notes.

A source (144 §3.1): read-only derived markdown of something fetched (file, URL, meeting, pasted
text, past session, MCP page, YouTube, audio, video) plus its insights. Bound by its origin key, so
the same thing is one document everywhere. Written by `Principal::Helper`/`File` only.

event.meeting_2eevents.output.CaptureFau.description: 173: why a capture track went quiet (the capture watchdog's episode reason).

oneOf.description:
Exact digital zeros for 15 s while sound played: a concurrent global-tap probe heard it
(per-app tap), or the source ran output (global tap, or a probe that could not open).
The OS refused the capture (System Audio Recording / Microphone permission).
The stream ended with an error (device lost, terminal error, reopen failed).

event.meeting_2eevents.output.CaptureHea.description:
173: one capture track as the user should hear about it. A track is `Ok` until the first
automatic reopen failed to bring audio back (or at once for a permission / terminal error),
so genuine silence never raises it. `since`: RFC 3339, when the track went quiet.

oneOf.description: Reopening; the first reopen did not help.
Three reopens did not help, or the OS refused: still retrying, the user should check.

reason.description: Why the app's tap was given up.

event.meeting_2eevents.output.Cleared.description: Why a `Detected` prompt went away (§4.4 rules 5 and 8).

oneOf.description: The user said "Not now": a 10-minute cooldown for that app.
The user said "Never for <App>": the app id joined `meeting.detect.ignore`.
The app released the mic for 30 s with nobody answering.
A meeting started (from the prompt or by hand).

No echo cancellation on the mic: the VoiceProcessingIO unit could not be opened (macOS), or
the OS has none (Windows/Linux — 58 §6.1's normal case). Headphones recommended (53 §0.4).
Live transcription of one track stopped (phase 2).
The meeting session's model is failing (phase 2).
Under 500 MB free on the data volume.
Documents run but refused the meeting's note (59 §7.4; the documents helper missing): no note, no summary note.

Live speaker labels stopped (07 §6): the diariser's session failed or its task
panicked; system lines are `them:` from here, the post pass still diarizes.

173: the app's tap stayed silent through three reopens while sound played (a probe
heard it, or the app ran output); the system track recorded every app on the default
output (minus theuth) from `at_ms`, until a return probe found the app's tap live again
at `until_ms` (`None`: to the end).

reason.description: Why the app's tap was given up.

until_ms.description: Recording-clock end, once the app's tap came back.

at_ms.description: ms since epoch of the derive.

ids_removed.description: Ids present before and not now, sorted.

207 §7: every item added or changed (content other than `score`/`reasons`/`alert`) since the previous
event, with `alert` set to `None` (alerts are per connection; see `alerts_changed`).

order.description: 207 §7: every listed id in engine order after this derive.

seq.description: 207 §7: 1-based per engine run, +1 per published event; 0 = an engine before 207.

event.roster_2eattention.output.Attentio.description: One inbox item. `id` is stable across derivations (dismiss / snooze key).

agent.description: The agent: hire / budget items, the task owner, else the desk the session belongs to (104 A3).

155 §7.1: the engine's alert decision for this item — set after
`roster.alert_delay_ms` for kinds that alert; rpc blanks it per
connection for the focused session and seen finishes (§7.3, §7.5).

ask.description: The pending question(s), for asks (104 A3): the screen renders at once.

at_ms.description: ms since epoch: when the item arose (task update, approval time, …).

blocks.description: 207 D5: sessions stopped behind this item (transitive `awaiting` on its session).

context.description:
149 E6: the conversation the item sits in, for session-born kinds
(ask, approval, finished, resume, blocked-with-session); `None` when
the session is unknown or has no messages.

deadline_ms.description: 207 R5: ms since epoch the request resolves itself (approval/ask/hand-off/secret timeout, a double's grace end).

detail.description: Why / what it waits on.

expires_ms.description: 207 R4: ms since epoch the item leaves the list on its own (`finished`: stop + `stopped_ttl_mins`).

next_steps.description: 130 E3: the agent's `## Next` list, ≤ 2 items of ≤ 80 chars (Finished items).

packet.description: The packet key (`decision:<id>` | `review:<task>`) when one exists (101): `packet_get` reads it.

parent_session.description: 207 R5: the item's session's parent; `None` for a root.

path.description: 207 R5: display path, root first: the root's title, then each child's peer name; empty when the session is unknown.

priority.description:
132 D4: the task's priority — task-born items and session items whose
session is a task checkout; `None` otherwise.

project.description: 207 R5: the session's effective project (its root's), else the task's; `None` when neither.

rank.description:
132 D4: [`tasks::rank::rank`] of that task (`project_order` step + priority
weight); `Priority::Medium.weight()` (5) for items without one. Higher first.

reasons.description: 207 D3: the score's contributors, points desc (ties in `AttentionSignal` order); `base` always present.

root_session.description: 207 R5: the root of the item's session tree (itself for a root).

score.description: 207 D3: the engine's score — the sum of `reasons`; the list is ordered by it (§3.4).

session.description: The session that produced the item, for every kind that has one (104 A3).

session_live.description: 207 R3: the item's session is running / awaiting / in approval right now.

stop.description: 207 R4: `finished` items — how the turn stopped.

summary.description: 130 E3: the first line of the turn's final text, ≤ 160 chars (Finished items).

tool.description: 207 R5: approvals — the tool name (`ApprovalRequested.tool`); `None` for other kinds.

turn.description: The turn the item belongs to, when the source carries one (104 A3). No source does yet.

waiting_since_ms.description:
130 E2: ms since epoch the user has been waited on — the approval's
arrival, the ask's arrival, the blocker's / review's `task_events`
time when known, else `at_ms`. `None` for kinds that wait on nobody.

event.roster_2eattention.output.Attentio.description: What kind of decision an item wants.

oneOf.description: A tool call waits for allow / deny.
A task is blocked on a `decision:<id>` — answer it.
A proposed agent waits for hire / decline.
A task is blocked on a person or another task.
A task in review with the user as reviewer — done or back.
An agent at ≥ 80 % of its month budget, or paused at the cap.
An agent in a VM needs a human at its desktop (79 §6.6): open it, then Done / Cancel.
A session asked for a secret (79 §6.6): the masked card, one or several fields.
A session asked the user a question (`ask_user`, 104 A1): answer or dismiss.
An agent showed the user an artifact (104 A1): see it.

109 §8.3: a session's interrupted turn needs a human — a replay
skipped a mutating call (effect unknown), an ACP child got a hand-off,
or `durability.resume: ask` waits for the Resume button.

126 §10: the double answered a card for the owner ("double answered
Allow for `git push` · undo 14 s"), or the daily L3 digest.

130 E3: a root or desk session's turn ended cleanly — the receipt, with
`summary` and the agent's `## Next` suggestions.

182 D9: a task's home engine is offline (or unknown) with tasks waiting
on it (`node:<engine id>`, raised by the lease holder) — move them here,
or keep waiting; nothing runs elsewhere on its own. S1: a task homed
here whose agent lives elsewhere (`misplaced:<task>`).

alerts_changed.description: 207 §7: some item's `alert` appeared, changed or went away: refetch `attention_list` (masked per connection).

at_ms.description: ms since epoch of the derive.

epoch_ms.description: 207 §7: ms since epoch the `Attention` actor started (a new value = a new run; `seq` restarts).

ids_removed.description: Ids present before and not now, sorted.

order.description: 207 §7: every listed id in engine order after this derive.

seq.description: 207 §7: 1-based per engine run, +1 per published event; 0 = an engine before 207.

agent.description: The agent: hire / budget items, the task owner, else the desk the session belongs to (104 A3).

alert.description:

connection for the focused session and seen finishes (§7.3, §7.5).

ask.description: The pending question(s), for asks (104 A3): the screen renders at once.

at_ms.description: ms since epoch: when the item arose (task update, approval time, …).

blocks.description: 207 D5: sessions stopped behind this item (transitive `awaiting` on its session).

context.description:
149 E6: the conversation the item sits in, for session-born kinds
(ask, approval, finished, resume, blocked-with-session); `None` when
the session is unknown or has no messages.

deadline_ms.description: 207 R5: ms since epoch the request resolves itself (approval/ask/hand-off/secret timeout, a double's grace end).

detail.description: Why / what it waits on.

expires_ms.description: 207 R4: ms since epoch the item leaves the list on its own (`finished`: stop + `stopped_ttl_mins`).

next_steps.description: 130 E3: the agent's `## Next` list, ≤ 2 items of ≤ 80 chars (Finished items).

packet.description: The packet key (`decision:<id>` | `review:<task>`) when one exists (101): `packet_get` reads it.

parent_session.description: 207 R5: the item's session's parent; `None` for a root.

path.description: 207 R5: display path, root first: the root's title, then each child's peer name; empty when the session is unknown.

priority.description:
132 D4: the task's priority — task-born items and session items whose
session is a task checkout; `None` otherwise.

project.description: 207 R5: the session's effective project (its root's), else the task's; `None` when neither.

rank.description:
132 D4: [`tasks::rank::rank`] of that task (`project_order` step + priority
weight); `Priority::Medium.weight()` (5) for items without one. Higher first.

reasons.description: 207 D3: the score's contributors, points desc (ties in `AttentionSignal` order); `base` always present.

root_session.description: 207 R5: the root of the item's session tree (itself for a root).

score.description: 207 D3: the engine's score — the sum of `reasons`; the list is ordered by it (§3.4).

session.description: The session that produced the item, for every kind that has one (104 A3).

session_live.description: 207 R3: the item's session is running / awaiting / in approval right now.

stop.description: 207 R4: `finished` items — how the turn stopped.

summary.description: 130 E3: the first line of the turn's final text, ≤ 160 chars (Finished items).

tool.description: 207 R5: approvals — the tool name (`ApprovalRequested.tool`); `None` for other kinds.

turn.description: The turn the item belongs to, when the source carries one (104 A3). No source does yet.

waiting_since_ms.description:
130 E2: ms since epoch the user has been waited on — the approval's
arrival, the ask's arrival, the blocker's / review's `task_events`
time when known, else `at_ms`. `None` for kinds that wait on nobody.

event.rpc_2estream.output.AlwaysAskWhy.description:
Why a call is always ask (219 §2.2, 221 D10): it raises a card even with approvals off,
and only a human may answer it.

oneOf.description:
Always-ask entries (`tools.always_ask` or a chat's list) that name the tool, its MCP
server (`mcp:<server>`), or an external secret connection the call reads or writes
(`secret:<backend>/<conn>:<direction>`). Sorted. Removing them stops the prompt.
The call writes theuth's own `config.yaml` or `mcp/config.yaml` (219 §2.4). Mandatory.

An MCP-admin tool while any always-ask entry applies, so re-registering a server cannot
shed its marks (219 §2.4). Mandatory while entries exist.

The chat's stored always-ask list could not be read, so every `Mutating` or riskier
call asks until it is (219 §3.2). Mandatory.

event.rpc_2estream.output.ApprovalReques.description: Event: a tool call is waiting on a human. Every UI subscribes.

always_ask.description:
219 §2.3: the tool is marked always ask: a human must answer, even with approvals
off. [`ResolveBy`] with any answerer but [`Answerer::Human`] is refused and the double
skips the card. Unlike `human_only`, any human surface may answer.

always_ask_why.description:
Why the call is always ask (set exactly when `always_ask` is): the marked entries that
matched, or the mandatory gate. Cards name it so an always-ask prompt with approvals
off is never unexplained (a `shell` reading a Bitwarden secret asks because of
`secret:bw/<conn>:read`, not because `shell` is marked).

args.description: Raw arguments; UIs format these per tool (shell: `command`).

human_only.description:
210 §7.2 (D10): only the owner, in person, may answer: every client renders an
owner-only card ("only you can answer"), a chat channel accepts only the owner's
click, and [`ResolveBy`] with any answerer but [`Answerer::Human`] is refused.

risk.description: Risk class that triggered the ask.

initiator.description: The engine that minted it; `""` for the legacy key.

members.description: Engines it was minted for or granted to (W-34).

count.description: Frames discarded by the ring or this subscription's backlog.

event.rpc_2estream.output.PendingPrompts.description:
The first item of every `subscribe_events` stream: every approval,
`ask_user` and `secret_request` still waiting on a user, filtered like the
live events. A client subscribing (or reconnecting over the relay) after
the `*Requested` broadcast still gets the card, and one that missed the
`*Resolved` drops it: after this item the client's pending set is exactly
what the engine reports (31 §7.3).

device_reset_pending.description:

old_destroyed.description: The previous key is retired here.

removed.description: Engines whose unpair started it; empty for a manual rotation.

removed_names.description:

rows_done.description: Rows already under the new key.

rows_stuck.description: Secret names whose rows open under no held key (§13 row 41).

sweep_hold_until_ms.description: 183 R4: the sweep hold's end (ms; [`Vault::rotate`]), kept so a restart still holds.

current.description: `Some(v)` when the name exists: the answer adds `v + 1`.

name.description: Vault name the answer is stored under.

note.description:

fields.description: Every field, in card order; one entry for `secret_request`.

name.description: Name the (first) field is stored under.

note.description: What it is for (the form's title when there is one).

oneOf.description: The request was answered, declined or timed out; frontends drop the field.
183 §10.4 (D7): a rotation minted, swept, reached a peer, finished or failed.

221 §9.4: a call needs a locked connection; frontends show the unlock card and answer

The unlock card was answered, declined or timed out; frontends drop it.

event.tools_2ejobs.output.JobEvent.description:
Bus events. `Output` is coalesced to one per [`OUTPUT_EVERY`] per job and
lossy under a flood; the log file is the truth. PTY jobs (22 §4.8) publish
`Screen` (coalesced the same way) instead of `Output`, and `Idle` when the
screen has stopped changing (61). Wire tags are `JobStarted` | `JobOutput`
| `JobScreen` | `JobIdle` | `JobFinished` so they read unambiguously on
the shared RPC event stream.

call_id.description: The `shell` call that started it: UIs attach live output to its card.

kind.description:
145 §0.4: `Promoted` for a tool call that outlived `promote_after`
(`command` is the tool name); `Shell` / `Pty` otherwise.

log.description: Log file receiving stdout+stderr as they arrive.

chunk.description: Lossy UTF-8 of the new bytes.

oneOf.description:
A PTY job's rendered screen (22 §4.3): blank trailing rows dropped,
rows right-trimmed. Not published for pipe jobs.

rows.description: Non-blank prefix of the 40 screen rows.

oneOf.description:
A running PTY job's screen has not changed for `quiet_secs` (61 §1).
Observation only on the bus: the model is woken through the activity
guard (`Notice::JobIdle`), never from here.

nudge.description: 1 for the first nudge of a backoff run, then 2, 3… (61 §1.4).

output.description: The screen text with its `cursor:` line: the `<job_idle>` body.

quiet_secs.description: Seconds since the screen last changed.

user_typed_secs.description: Seconds since a human typed into the job, within the 55 §2.3 window.

why.description:
155 §6.5: why it fired — `screen unchanged for N s, process tree
quiet` or `no reaction to input`. Empty from older engines.

oneOf.description:
The job ended; the agent injects this as `<job_result>` unless `inline`.
A [`CancelJob`] kill shapes it by [`CancelOrigin`] (14 §1.2 as-built):
`Tool` → `inline: true` (the `cancel_job` reply was the acknowledgement,
the model already read the screen it killed — 61); `Ui` / `Shutdown` →
injected, `output` a one-line notice. Never the screen or the log.

inline.description:
The tool call already returned this result (exited within the
grace window), or the model killed it; UIs still count it, the
agent must not inject it.

kind.description: 145 §0.4: `Promoted` → the agent wraps it as `<job_result tool="…">`.

output.description:
stdout+stderr, truncated to 64 KiB; the agent applies spill. For
a PTY job the final screen text (22 §2.2). For a `Killed` job the
origin's [`CancelOrigin::notice`].

pty.description: Ran on a pseudo-terminal (22): `output` is a screen, not a log.

secs.description: Wall time from spawn to exit.

oneOf.description: The command returned this code (a shell error is `1`).

The job's deadline (`tools.job_timeout_secs`, or the call's shorter
`timeout_secs`) elapsed; the process group was killed.

[`CancelJob`] killed the process group; the [`CancelOrigin`] decides
what the model hears about it.

109 §5.4: the job died with the engine (or was reaped after a
SIGKILL leaked it); its exit code is unknown. Never produced by a
running job — written by the journal's reaper and the shutdown path.

145 §0.4: an inline tool call that outlived `promote_after`; `command`
is the tool name, there is no process and no log.

method.a2a.input.ContactPatch.description:

191: replaced by `grant` / `revoke`; a patch that sets it is refused
([`EXPORTS_REPLACED`]), never read as a whole list (it revoked every grant its
machine could not see).

full_access.description: 200 (D1): give or take back full access (every record of the group).

grant.description: Export names (or ids) to grant; every other grant stays.

revoke.description: Export names (or ids) to take back; every other grant stays.

the mesh (191: a second one is renamed `<name>-2`).

paused.description: W-41: why the export answers nothing now: `chat archived` | `agent messaging off`.

oneOf.description:

agent's own `tools:` ceiling (W-25).

agent.description: `<agent>@<engine>` desk root, or `theuth`.

peer.description: The one peer granted this export.

method.a2a.output.A2aPeerStatus.description: One configured peer as the owner sees it.

method.a2a.output.A2aStatus.description: Network status for `/a2a` and settings (§10). Never carries a credential.

error.description:
Config/listener/reload problem; `None` when healthy. A failed reload
keeps the previous configuration live and reports why here.

listening.description: The loopback listener is bound (needs global communication on).

method.a2a.output.Contact.description: One contact as Settings › Network › Contacts shows it (`contact_list`).

exports.description:
Export names granted to it, mesh-wide (191: from the records, a chat on another
machine too; a waiting or refused contact's as well).

fingerprint.description: §7.3: the endpoint id in groups of 4 base32 characters, first 20 characters.

first_contact.description: Export → first-contact answer; a missing export is `ask`.

full_access.description: 200 (D1): we gave it full access: any of its sessions may list and message ours.

full_access_from.description:
200 (D11): whether it gave us full access, from its last verified card; `None` when
its card lacks the `full-access/v1` extension (an engine without 200).

full_capable.description: 186 (D10): its card advertises [`EXT_FULL`]. Shown only: a share never depends on it.

id.description: 191 (D2): its record id (the same on every machine of the mesh).

machine.description: The contact's machine, from its card.

machines.description:
191 (D8): the contact's machines as THIS machine accepted them (its own roster state,
never a replicated row): the current roster, then those its accepted history lists
but the roster no longer does (`left`); the pins while no roster is based here.

name.description: Owner alias: the `peer:<name>` address; 191: the record's alias, unique in the mesh.

paired_ms.description: When the ceremony finished (ms since epoch).

paired_on.description:
191 (D8): the machine of ours whose ceremony paired it, by its name (`contact_list`
names the record's engine id: the first 8 characters once that machine left the
mesh); `None` when no machine is recorded (an import).

path.description: How it is reached right now.

problem.description:
191 (D2): why this machine quarantined the record (it is refused, its endpoints
denied), or D1's inflation alert on a live one; `None` for a sound one.

problem_kind.description: 191 (D8): what the row offers for its `problem`; `None` exactly when it has none.

shared.description:
183 F1: what the contact shares with us (its exports granted to this engine), from
the card it last served us.

method.a2a.output.ContactMachine.description: 191 (D8): one machine of a contact, as this machine knows it.

left.description: In this machine's accepted history of the contact's roster, not in its current one.

name.description:
The `machine` of its last card this machine fetched (in memory), else the first 8
characters of `eid`.

method.a2a.output.ContactOffer.description: 183 §7.7 (F1): one export a contact grants this engine, from the card it serves us.

mode.description: 186: the mode the contact granted us this export in.

state.description: Whether a message goes through now.

method.a2a.output.ContactWindow.description: `contact_window(true)`: the open Add contact window's invite ticket.

expires_ms.description: When the window and the ticket expire (ms since epoch).

ticket.description: `theuth-contact:1.…`, for the QR and the copy button.

method.a2a.output.EngineId.description: An engine's identity: its iroh endpoint id (an Ed25519 public key) as text.

id.description: 191 (D2): its replicated id; `None` on a new export (`a2a_export_put` mints one).

name.description:
Export name: the card skill and the `/agents/<name>` path, `[a-z0-9_-]`, unique in
the mesh (191: a second one is renamed `<name>-2`).

paused.description: W-41: why the export answers nothing now: `chat archived` | `agent messaging off`.

oneOf.description:
One of this machine's agents: an inbox per (contact, export) that runs under the
agent's own `tools:` ceiling (W-25).

agent.description: `<agent>@<engine>` desk root, or `theuth`.

oneOf.description: One chat of any machine in the mesh: the contact's messages arrive as a mesh peer's.

method.a2a.output.FirstContact.description: 183 §9.4: a contact's first-contact answer for one export. Absent = `ask`.

oneOf.description: Raise the Attention item; the task waits in `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`.

method.a2a.output.FirstWaiting.description:
183 F3, F11: one (contact, export) whose first message waits for the owner's answer
(`contact_first_waiting`), the same source as the `contact_first` Attention item.

export.description: The export it wants to reach.

machine.description: The contact's machine, from its card (`""` when unknown).

position.description: 186 review 1: a queued message's place in the chat's queue (1 = next); `0` for a hold.

preview.description: The first line of the oldest one.

queued.description:
186 review 1: not a first-contact hold but a message admitted and waiting behind the
chat's running turn (it starts when that turn ends); only `contact_first_waiting` lists
these, never the Attention item.
An older engine sends neither field (TS: optional).

session.description: The session its message would run in (the exported chat, or the agent's inbox).

since_ms.description: When the oldest waiting message arrived (ms since epoch).

method.a2a.output.NearbyAgent.description: `contact_nearby`: one A2A agent the browse saw (a hint, never stored, §7.1).

addr.description: The address it was seen at.

service.description: The service type it was seen under (`_a2a._tcp`, …).

verified.description: The fetched card's JWS verified against the endpoint id in its iroh interface.

method.a2a.output.OfferKind.description: 183 §7.7 (F1): what one export a contact offers us is.

oneOf.description: One of the contact's chats: our messages arrive there as a mesh peer's.
One of the contact's agents: its inbox for us.

method.a2a.output.OfferState.description:
183 §7.7 (F1): whether a message to an offered export goes through now, as the sharer
reported it on its card.

oneOf.description: The first message waits until the owner presses Allow, then goes through.
Answers nothing right now (chat archived, or its messaging off).

method.a2a.output.PairCeremony.description: 183 §6.8: one Nearby pairing ceremony, as both sides show it.

addr.description:
Where the other engine is: the advert's address (dialer) or the connection's remote
address (acceptor); `""` when unknown. A contact ceremony (§7.4): the contact's
machine, from its card.

expires_ms.description: When the ceremony expires (ms since epoch).

method.a2a.output.PeerPath.description: 183 §3.3: how a peer is reached right now.

method.a2a.output.ProblemKind.description: 191 (D8): what a contact row with a `problem` offers.

oneOf.description: Refused here and it will not mend itself: Remove is the action.
Held while replication catches up: no action, it clears by itself.
D1's inflation alert: the contact still works; Remove, or unpair one of ours.

method.a2a.output.SessionId.description: Identifies a conversation; every event carries one.

method.a2a.output.ShareMode.description:
186 (D1): how a contact share collaborates. 190: every share is `Full`: the contact's
message arrives like a mesh peer's, the receiving agent replies with
`send_message(reply_to)` any number of times and the chat's own tool policy applies.
`Cautious` (183's one capped turn per message, the reply the turn text) is only read: from
old rows and an older contact's card (absent = cautious).

body.description: The body as the router wrote it (JSON-RPC text, or empty).

status.description: HTTP status (a JSON-RPC error rides inside a 200).

method.agent.input.BroadcastRequest.description:
One message to many sessions (62 §0.1); `ask` the supervisor with
[`Broadcast`] → `Result<BroadcastReceipt, String>`.

delivery.description: How it lands on a busy recipient.

dry_run.description: Resolve and report the rows without sending.

files.description: Image files (17 §2); copied per recipient by path.

text.description: User text; stored behind a `[broadcast <id> · <n> sessions]` marker line.

oneOf.description:
Roots that are active themselves or have an active descendant subagent
(child, grandchild, …; advisors excluded). Active = state `Running |
Awaiting | Approval` or `jobs + ptys > 0`. Never names a subagent.
Every root with a live actor.
Explicit ids, roots or children; order kept, duplicates dropped.

method.agent.input.CancelReason.description:
Why a turn is cancelled: `Input` (the owner's interject or flush) or `Stop` (the default,
an explicit Stop). 190 (D5): accepted and ignored; either cancels any turn, a contact's
included.

oneOf.description: The owner's input interrupting the turn.
The target session only; its running descendants keep working. The default.
The target and every running descendant (design doc 19 §2.3).

method.agent.input.CompactStyle.description: How a compaction builds the new epoch head (design doc 11).

oneOf.description: Drop the folded span, keep the tail, no model call.
Rasterize the folded span to images. Named in v0; not built.

`/clear` (11 §2.4): fold everything, keep nothing, no model call. Manual only —
never a default or automatic style.

method.agent.input.CompactorProfile.description:
201 §7.1: the compactor profile. Named `CompactorProfile` on the wire
(TypeScript, JSON schema): `meeting` already exports a `Profile`.

oneOf.description: `small` for a local model or a known window of at most 32_000 tokens, else `standard`.
One unit per call, short prompt and reply (§7.2).

method.agent.input.ContextLevel.description: The context dial (144 §5.1): how much of an item the model sees in a thread.

oneOf.description: Not in the context at all.

method.agent.input.ContextOwner.description: Which stored row a binary occurrence lives in.

method.agent.input.ContextTarget.description:
A removable occurrence, addressed by stored coordinates (48 §3.1). `part`
and `image` index the **original** arrays, never the filtered ones.

oneOf.description: One binary part, or one image inside a tool response part.

image.description: `Some`: index into the `ToolResponse.images` of that part.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts.

oneOf.description: One surface fence inside one text part of an assistant row (197 §3).

index.description: 0-based ordinal of the surface fences of that original text part ([`surface_fences`]).

owner.description: The row; only `Message` owners have fences.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts (a text part).

oneOf.description: The source argument of one `show` / `app` / `page_preview` call part (197 §3).

owner.description: The row; only `Message` owners have sources.

part.description: Index into the row's original content parts (a tool call part).

method.agent.input.CostBasis.description: Where a cell's money comes from (160 D5).

oneOf.description: An external harness reported the money (remote meters).
theuth's price table × tokens (`estimated_*`, or repriced at read time).

method.agent.input.CostCallsCursor.description: Keyset position in the calls ledger (exclusive).

before.description: Exclusive cursor: rows strictly older than it.

roots.description: Root session ids (the UI maps owner / project / session filters to roots).

method.agent.input.CostCubeCursor.description: A cube state the client already holds.

method.agent.input.Delivery.description:
How a human input lands on a busy session (62 §0.3): `Steer` joins the
running turn after the current tool batch; `NextTurn` waits for the turn to
end. An idle session starts a turn now either way.

oneOf.description: Inject after the current tool batch (today's behaviour).
Hold until the running turn ends; opens the next one.

method.agent.input.DescribeImages.description: 201 §8: whether an image leaving the tail gets a one-line description.

oneOf.description: Never described; the unit keeps its name only.

method.agent.input.DocId.description:
A document id: 26 lowercase base32 characters (§4.1). Bound documents (knowledge, artifact,
meeting note) render uuid v5 of the binding key under [`DocId::NAMESPACE`], so every engine of a
mesh mints the same id for the same thing (69 §5); notes, which have no natural key, render uuid v7.

method.agent.input.EndlessConfig.description:
`agent.endless` (137 §11.1). Every key optional in YAML; the whole struct
is what Settings › Memory reads and writes (`endless_settings_get/set`).

age_by_use.description: 201 §10: a zoomed line stays unmerged for one generation.

attempt_secs.description: 137F E6: one attempt's bound in seconds for a cloud compactor (10..=3600).

backfill_max_units.description: R1-D4: at switch-on the tree covers only the last this many units.

batch_units.description: 137G G6: consecutive unsummarized units one compactor call summarizes (1..=64).

cap_chars.description: Tool-result cap in chars before a unit is cut head ⅔ / tail ⅓ (§4).

cold_after_secs.description:
201 §4.3: idle seconds after which a trim is taken early (0..=86_400);
0 = the transport's cache lifetime.

compactor_ctx_bytes.description: 137G G3: the compactor's `<chat>` context cap in bytes for every model (8_000..=256_000); a local one takes the smaller of this and `local_ctx_bytes`.

default_desk.description: Desks without an explicit `memory:` field (R1-D7: on).

describe_images.description: 201 §8: one-line description when an image leaves the tail (`auto` | `off`).

effort.description:
194: the compactor model's effort; `None` = thinking off (R1 Q1). Only
with `model` (validated against it, dropped when a new `model` does not take it).

jobs.description: Compactor calls in flight per session.

ledger.description: 201 §9: the state ledger and its tool.

ledger_suggestions.description: 201 §9: summary-model flags shown as unconfirmed suggestions.

local_attempt_secs.description: 137F E6: one attempt's bound in seconds for a local compactor (30..=7200).

local_ctx_bytes.description: 137F E8: a local compactor sees at most this many bytes of the `<chat>` view, newest kept (4_000..=256_000).

local_jobs.description: 137F E9: compactor calls in flight per local endpoint, engine-wide (1..=16).

max_usd_per_call.description: 137G G11: USD one compactor call's prompt may cost (0.001..=10); over it the context shrinks, else the line folds mechanically.

max_usd_per_session_day.description: 137G G11: USD a chat's compactor may spend per UTC day (0..=1000, 0 = no cap); reaching it pauses settling (`paused_by: "spend"`).

meeting_view_bytes.description: View budget for a meeting head's `## Earlier in this meeting` (R1-D6).

merge_at.description: 201 §6: share of `view_bytes` at which merges start being built (0.50..=1.00).

model.description: Compactor model; `None` = the session's own model (D8).

node_bytes.description: One summary line's ceiling in bytes.

prefetch_bytes.description: 201 §10: recall hits appended to the input, in bytes (0..=8_000); 0 = off.

raw_bytes.description: 137G G2: unsummarized lines the view shows verbatim, newest first, in bytes (4_000..=128_000); older ones fold into one placeholder line.

retry_secs.description: Delay before a failed node is retried.

settle_secs.description: How long a turn waits for the view to be fully built (D10).

slack.description: Slack band of the fold (0.0..=0.5), D5.

tail_high_bytes.description: 201 §4.2 fixed mode: where a trim is due (16_000..=512_000); above the low mark.

tail_high_share.description: 201 §4.2 scaled mode: high mark as a share (0.05..=0.60); above the low share.

tail_low_bytes.description: 201 §4.2 fixed mode: verbatim context kept after a trim (8_000..=256_000).

tail_low_share.description: 201 §4.2 scaled mode: low mark as a share of the session model's turn allowance (0.02..=0.40).

tail_mode.description: 201 §4.2: how the verbatim tail is sized (`fixed` | `scaled`).

tries.description: Attempts per node before the best candidate wins (D7).

view_bytes.description: View budget in bytes (16_000..=256_000; R1-D2: 128 KB).

method.agent.input.GatewayProtocol.description: `protocol:` of a `providers.yaml` row: which genai adapter speaks to the endpoint.

method.agent.input.GraphCursor.description: 208 §4: where a client is in the delta stream.

method.agent.input.InputId.description:
One user input, identified by its sender so it can be shown before any
reply arrives.

method.agent.input.InsightInstruction.description:
What `insight_run` should produce (144 §4.3): exactly one of a builtin (`key_insights` | `toc` |
`open_questions`) or a skill whose front matter has `notebook_insight: true`.

oneOf.description: A `SessionId` (owner-only; never covered by the derived share grant, D13).

method.agent.input.JobCursor.description: Exclusive position in job history, ordered by start time then id, both descending.

id.description: The last returned job's id, breaking ties at the same millisecond.

started_ms.description: The last returned job's start time, unix milliseconds.

method.agent.input.Key.description:
A key `send` (and a human over `pty_input`, 55 §2.2) types. Encoded by
[`encode`], which consults the screen's modes: arrows follow
application-cursor mode, `paste` is bracketed only when the program asked.

oneOf.description: Ctrl + a letter or one of `@ [ \ ] ^ _`.

method.agent.input.LocalRuntime.description: 177: a local model runtime preset. `openai` = a generic OpenAI-compatible local server.

method.agent.input.McpRef.description: One MCP call a source is fetched by.

oneOf.description: 07/11 epochs: carried transcript, folded into summary heads.
137: the summary tree and its view.
One page, every claim a chip → `briefing.md`.

method.agent.input.PeerEnvelope.description:
One peer message on the wire between engines (69 P): what the sender's
supervisor forwards to the owner of the addressed session as
`peer_deliver(session, envelope)` over `theuth/rpc/1`. `id` is the
sender's minted message id, kept by the owner's intake so `reply_to`
names the same message on both engines.

chain.description:
183 §6.5: the sender's chain count, so the 256 limit holds across
engines; 0 from an older sender.

from.description: Authenticated sender session (a row every replica holds).

id.description: The message id, minted on the sender's engine.

method.agent.input.PeerScope.description:
Root communication scope (§2.3): who may discover a tree from outside it.
Children inherit their root's scope dynamically.

oneOf.description: Owner-console root: may exchange with other `owner` roots.

Reachable only inside its own tree. The default and the migration
value for roots of unknown provenance.

method.agent.input.PressToken.description:
What the UI passes with a call an owner press started. Advisory only: authority is the
engine the app is connected to, which forwards the press only when its own
`human_press` check of the calling connection passes.

at.description: When the press happened (ms since epoch).

id.description: Client-chosen id (a uuid); stable across machines.

name.description: Shown in the `+` menu and the chip.

text.description: Appended to a message after a blank line.

method.agent.input.ProviderRow.description:
One `providers.yaml` row as a mesh copy carries it (`sync_providers` → the target's
`apply_providers`). `key` is sent only when the copy asked for keys; otherwise the target uses
the vault secret of `name` it already has (the vault replicates).

account_of.description: An account instance of this login kind (`anthropic`), not a gateway.

grant.description: An account's login grant (`oauth/<name>`, JSON), only when the copy includes keys.

key.description: The API key, only when the copy includes keys.

name.description: The provider's name (`rwx` → `rwx/model`); also its vault secret's name.

owns_key.description: R2-3: the vault secret of `name` is this provider's own (its add stored it).

protocol.description: The row's hand-set wire protocol; `None`: by host.

runtime.description: 177: the runtime preset it was added with.

method.agent.input.PtyViewport.description: Which rows of the retained terminal a [`PtyScreen`] asks for.

oneOf.description:
`height` (≤ 80) scrollback rows whose bottom is `offset` rows above
the live screen's top; clamped to what is retained.

method.agent.output.DocId.description:
A document id: 26 lowercase base32 characters (§4.1). Bound documents (knowledge, artifact,
meeting note) render uuid v5 of the binding key under [`DocId::NAMESPACE`], so every engine of a
mesh mints the same id for the same thing (69 §5); notes, which have no natural key, render uuid v7.

oneOf.description: A knowledge concept; the derived file is `knowledge/<id>.md` and the first block is the frontmatter.
An agent's charter — the body of `agents/<name>.md` (67 §6.1); the roster copies each export into the file.

A task's thread (67 §7.1): comments, answers and the event log of one task. Owned by the task,
so it never lists as a note.

A board (71 §2.1): a note the agent draws for a reader — sections, anchored prose, `Excerpt`s and
diagrams — bound like a note (`Binding::Note`, `documents/<id>/note.md`); its first block is the
frontmatter carrying `root:`, the absolute repository root every `code:` link and `ref` resolves against.

A notebook (144 §3.1): the container over notes, sources, sessions and artifacts. Its body is the
description the agent reads as a prompt block; its lists are `notebook_items` rows. Never lists
among notes.

A source (144 §3.1): read-only derived markdown of something fetched (file, URL, meeting, pasted
text, past session, MCP page, YouTube, audio, video) plus its insights. Bound by its origin key, so
the same thing is one document everywhere. Written by `Principal::Helper`/`File` only.

project.description: Project label the note or board is filed under (the sessions' vocabulary, one level); `None` = ungrouped.
