agent.description: The agent: hire / budget items, the task owner, else the desk the session belongs to (104 A3).

alert.description:

ask.description: The pending question(s), for asks (104 A3): the screen renders at once.

blocks.description: 207 D5: sessions stopped behind this item (transitive `awaiting` on its session).

context.description:

next_steps.description: 130 E3: the agent's `## Next` list, ≤ 2 items of ≤ 80 chars (Finished items).

packet.description: The packet key (`decision:<id>` | `review:<task>`) when one exists (101): `packet_get` reads it.

parent_session.description: 207 R5: the item's session's parent; `None` for a root.

A task is blocked on a `decision:<id>` — answer it.

A task is blocked on a person or another task.

An agent at ≥ 80 % of its month budget, or paused at the cap.

An agent showed the user an artifact (104 A1): see it.

109 §8.3: a session's interrupted turn needs a human — a replay
skipped a mutating call (effect unknown), an ACP child got a hand-off,
or `durability.resume: ask` waits for the Resume button.

Allow for `git push` · undo 14 s"), or the daily L3 digest.

`summary` and the agent's `## Next` suggestions.

182 D9: a task's home engine is offline (or unknown) with tasks waiting

here whose agent lives elsewhere (`misplaced:<task>`).

the two `allow_private_network` keys behind Network's "Local network
access" (16 §5, amended 2026-11-11), 212 §15's switches, which apply to new

sentence and its reminders. Applies to new sessions, no restart.

Applies to new sessions, no restart.

skipped. UI state only, nothing in the engine reads it; absent is `false`. No restart.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.ConfigFlag.description: 188: a [`ConfigFlagKey`] as config.yaml holds it and as this engine runs it.

enabled.description: The value `<data_dir>/config.yaml` holds now (the section's default when absent).

restart_required.description:

`false` for a 212 §15 switch and `onboarding.completed`.

running.description:

restart. A 212 §15 switch (`agent.status_tool`, `agent.auto_title`, `agent.suggestions`, `knowledge.peek`)

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.ConfigFlagKe.description:
188: the flags Settings had no write path for: four `<section>.enabled` and
the two `allow_private_network` keys behind Network's "Local network
access" (16 §5, amended 2026-11-11), 212 §15's switches, which apply to new
sessions without a restart, and 215's `onboarding.completed`. Any other string
fails to deserialize, an `INVALID_PARAMS` error listing these.

oneOf.description: `decision.enabled` (57 §7.1): off, the decision actor escalates every ask.
`computer.enabled` (27): the computer-use actor, tools and input thread.

`double.enabled` (126): the double actors, tools and prompt paragraph. Its own
`double_settings_set` needs the running scheduler, so it cannot turn it on.
`web.allow_private_network`: the web tools reach the local network.
`browser.allow_private_network`: the browser reaches the local network.

`agent.status_tool` (212 §15): new sessions get `set_status`, its prompt
sentence and its reminders. Applies to new sessions, no restart.

`agent.auto_title` (212 §15): the title model names and renames new sessions.
Applies to new sessions, no restart.

`agent.suggestions`: "What's next?" suggestions after interactive chat turns.
Applies to new sessions, no restart.

`knowledge.peek` (212 §15): new sessions list `peek_memory` and its hint and
prompt sentences; off, its calls are refused at once. No restart.

`onboarding.completed` (215): the desktop's first-run wizard was finished or
skipped. UI state only, nothing in the engine reads it; absent is `false`. No restart.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.Coverage.description: How much of the selected source a ready page actually searched.

oneOf.description: Some records or content could not be searched; see `notices`.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.DocId.description:
A document id: 26 lowercase base32 characters (§4.1). Bound documents (knowledge, artifact,
meeting note) render uuid v5 of the binding key under [`DocId::NAMESPACE`], so every engine of a
mesh mints the same id for the same thing (69 §5); notes, which have no natural key, render uuid v7.

oneOf.description: A knowledge concept; the derived file is `knowledge/<id>.md` and the first block is the frontmatter.
An agent's charter — the body of `agents/<name>.md` (67 §6.1); the roster copies each export into the file.

A task's thread (67 §7.1): comments, answers and the event log of one task. Owned by the task,
so it never lists as a note.

A board (71 §2.1): a note the agent draws for a reader — sections, anchored prose, `Excerpt`s and
diagrams — bound like a note (`Binding::Note`, `documents/<id>/note.md`); its first block is the
frontmatter carrying `root:`, the absolute repository root every `code:` link and `ref` resolves against.

A notebook (144 §3.1): the container over notes, sources, sessions and artifacts. Its body is the
description the agent reads as a prompt block; its lists are `notebook_items` rows. Never lists
among notes.

A source (144 §3.1): read-only derived markdown of something fetched (file, URL, meeting, pasted
text, past session, MCP page, YouTube, audio, video) plus its insights. Bound by its origin key, so
the same thing is one document everywhere. Written by `Principal::Helper`/`File` only.

project.description: Project label the note or board is filed under (the sessions' vocabulary, one level); `None` = ungrouped.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.HistorySearc.description: One `(change commit, concept)` record that matched (49 §3.4).

parent.description: Full first-parent id; `None` for a root commit.

snapshot_commit.description:
The commit whose tree holds the matched body (`commit` for After, the
parent for Before); `None` for a metadata hit.

status.description: How the commit touched the concept file.

title.description: Title in the change commit, else in the parent, else the id.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.HistorySide.description: Which candidate of a historical change matched.

oneOf.description: The complete text in the first parent.
The complete text in the change commit.
Concept id, frontmatter and commit subject.

method.rpc_2dcompose.output.Info.description:
Reply to `info`: what a client needs before its first session (25 §7);
the in-process TUI reads the same things off the [`runtime::Runtime`] directly.

advisor.description:
125 §6.5: the advisor's remembered pick and tuning keys (`advisor:` section).
Absent from an older harness → defaults.

app_enabled.description:
The app plugin is running (`app.enabled`, 46 §9): `get_app`/`app_*`
answer and the `app` tool exists. `false` leaves app artifacts
readable as source only. Absent from an older harness → `false`.

auto_archive_after_secs.description: `agent.auto_archive.after` in seconds (default 14 days). `0` from an older harness.

auto_archive_enabled.description:
`agent.auto_archive.enabled`: root chats with no event for
`auto_archive_after_secs` are archived. `false` from an older harness.

communication.description:
The global communication switch (50 §10): `session: None`, the
authoritative ceiling every per-session state inherits.

default_effort.description:
`agent.effort`: the reasoning effort new sessions start on (live, 83 §3);
`None` = the provider default. Absent from an older harness → `None`.

default_model.description: `agent.model`: the model new sessions start on (live, 82 §3).

favorite_models.description:
`agent.favorite_models` (127 §1): starred model ids in starring order,
shown first in every picker. Absent from an older harness → empty.

hint_limit.description:
`agent.knowledge.hint_limit` (212 §15): concepts per memory hint for new
sessions; `0` = no hints. `0` from an older harness.

home_offline_ask_secs.description:
`tasks.home_offline_ask_secs` (182 D9): how long a task's home machine may be
offline, with tasks waiting on it, before the Attention item asks. `0` from an older harness.

max_salvages.description: `agent.max_salvages`: interrupted-reply recoveries per turn before it stops with an error.

max_tool_rounds.description: `agent.max_tool_rounds`: tool-call rounds a turn may run before the loop lands.

name.description:
Harness display name (`link.name`, else the hostname): what a linked
device shows in its harness switcher (31 §6.4).

peek_threshold.description:
`knowledge.peek_threshold` (212 §15): the live minimum P(true) for
`peek_memory` to call a memory relevant. `0` from an older harness.

platform.description:
Host OS (`std::env::consts::OS`: `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, …); a
parent shows it beside a node's name (32 §6.2).

pty_idle_secs.description: `tools.pty_idle_secs`: quiet-screen seconds before a PTY job wakes the model with `<job_idle>` (61); `0` = never.

schedule_run_timeout_secs.description:
`schedule.run_timeout_secs` (88): seconds a routine run may take before it is
cancelled and its history row says `timeout`; a routine's own `run_timeout:`
overrides it. `0` from an older harness.

status_every.description:
`agent.status_every` (212 §15): tool calls between status reminders for new
sessions; `0` = off. `0` from an older harness.

stream_idle_secs.description: `agent.stream_idle_secs`: seconds without a stream event before a model call is abandoned.

mesh mints the same id for the same thing (69 §5); notes, which have no natural key, render uuid v7.

oneOf.description: A knowledge concept; the derived file is `knowledge/<id>.md` and the first block is the frontmatter.
An agent's charter — the body of `agents/<name>.md` (67 §6.1); the roster copies each export into the file.

A task's thread (67 §7.1): comments, answers and the event log of one task. Owned by the task,
so it never lists as a note.

A board (71 §2.1): a note the agent draws for a reader — sections, anchored prose, `Excerpt`s and
diagrams — bound like a note (`Binding::Note`, `documents/<id>/note.md`); its first block is the
frontmatter carrying `root:`, the absolute repository root every `code:` link and `ref` resolves against.

A notebook (144 §3.1): the container over notes, sources, sessions and artifacts. Its body is the
description the agent reads as a prompt block; its lists are `notebook_items` rows. Never lists
among notes.

A source (144 §3.1): read-only derived markdown of something fetched (file, URL, meeting, pasted
text, past session, MCP page, YouTube, audio, video) plus its insights. Bound by its origin key, so
the same thing is one document everywhere. Written by `Principal::Helper`/`File` only.

method.sandbox.input.SandboxCreate.description: RPC + tool argument for a new VM. Every field optional except `name`; defaults from Preflight.defaults / VmDefaults.

method.sandbox.output.Blocker.description:
One reason a VM cannot (or should not) be created here.

`code` values: `unsupported_os` (Windows v1), `unsupported_arch` (x86_64 macOS: "microsandbox
needs Apple Silicon"), `no_kvm` ("/dev/kvm missing — enable virtualization in firmware, or nested
virtualization in the outer hypervisor"), `kvm_not_writable` ("add your user to the kvm group:
sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER, then log in again"), `glibc_too_old` ("needs glibc ≥ 2.28"),
`runtime_extract_failed` (the embedded pair could not be written into the home; retry),
`runtime_missing` (only when no runtime was built), `runtime_incomplete` ("msb X but libkrunfw Y"),
`disk_low` ("N GiB free; a VM needs root_disk + image + 2 GiB"), `memory_low` (warning: default
memory > host/2), `docker_missing` (warning, dev image path only), `runtime_home` (warning: theuth's
VMs live in a home the user's own `msb` does not look at), `vm_disabled` (`sandbox.vm.enabled: false`).

installable.description:
`true` only for `runtime_extract_failed` / `runtime_missing` / `runtime_incomplete`: the
**Set up runtime** button (`sandbox_install_runtime`) can clear it.

method.sandbox.output.DesktopAccess.description: What the pop-out needs to draw the desktop (RPC only, never a tool result).

method.sandbox.output.PendingView.description: What waits for the next start.

method.sandbox.output.Preflight.description:
Host readiness. `blockers` empty ⇒ a VM can be created now. Every blocker is user-facing:
`code` stable for the UI, `message` one sentence, `fix` what to do (or None when nothing can be done on this host).

oneOf.description:
The pair compiled into `t` (79 decision 2, embed ruling). `extracted: false` = the first
`create` (or `sandbox_install_runtime`) writes it into `home`; `true` = `home` holds that
version already (ours or the user's own install of the same version).

A user-provided pair of another version (`sandbox.vm.home`, `MSB_PATH`, or an `msb` on
`PATH`); used as is.
No runtime at all — only when `t` was built without one (`vm::runtime` failed).

method.sandbox.output.SandboxInfo.description: One sandbox record as the UI and `sandbox_list` see it.

method.sandbox.output.VmMetrics.description:
Live numbers from the hypervisor. `memory_limit_bytes` is the hypervisor's current
allocation (what a live resize changes); `memory_bytes` is the guest's use within it. The
guest's own `MemTotal` stays at the boot size by virtio-mem design and never tracks a
resize — not a bug; read the limit, not the guest.

mesh_port.description: Host loopback UDP port for iroh.

method.sessionsync.input.CreateSessionOp.description:
Options of `create_session`. `view` is the client's view id, required
for a private root (it names the single owner); `project` is root
metadata; `cwd` is recorded on the row.

advisor.description:
Advisor model/effort for this root. Installed on its owner before create
returns: `set_advisor` is local-only, so a remote draft cannot use it.

cap.description:
Risk ceiling for this root and its descendants (67 §8: a remote
parent's `tools`); installed on the registry like a subagent's cap.

cwd.description: Working directory recorded on the session row.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort for this session only; `None` = `agent.effort`. Like
`model`, never the default (a remote parent's pick, 67 §8).

engine.description:
183 §5.6 (W-10): the mesh engine id to create the session on; `None`
(or this engine) = here. The attached engine forwards the whole call.

harness.description:
Open the root as a child of this `acp/agents.yaml` harness of ours
instead of a native session (67 §8, `agent: "<harness>@<engine>"`
arriving as `_meta.theuth.harness`). `model` then goes through the
harness's model option; `effort` and `cap` do not apply.

model.description:
Model for this session only (catalog id); `None` = `agent.model`. Unlike
[`crate::SetModel`] it never rewrites the default or `config.yaml`
(`meetings/02-live.md` §0.2).

notebook.description: 144 §8: bind the new root to this notebook (`DocId` text); durable sessions only.

parent_engine.description: That engine's id as this one knows it (`_meta.theuth.parent_engine`).

parent_session.description:
The session on another engine that opens this root over the node conn
(67 §8, `_meta.theuth.parent`): it becomes this root's `parent` peer.

project.description: Root project label; `None` = ungrouped.

view.description: The client's view id; required for a private root, which it owns.

oneOf.description: 07/11 epochs: carried transcript, folded into summary heads.
137: the summary tree and its view.

method.sessionsync.input.Retention.description: What happens to a root tree's data when it closes.

oneOf.description: Persisted in the durable store and data dir.
In-memory store, scratch files; nothing survives the close (51 §4).

method.sessionsync.input.Risk.description: How much damage a tool can do; the only input to the approval policy.

oneOf.description: Changes state that can be undone or is scoped.
Irreversible or unbounded (arbitrary shell, delete, network writes).

method.sessionsync.input.SessionId.description: Identifies a conversation; every event carries one.

method.sessionsync.output.PeerSync.description:
`sessions_sync` entry: this engine's `theuth/sessions/1` session-log
replication with one peer, from memory (no store read). Seqs are log
positions: ours of our own log, the peer's of its own.

acked.description: How far of our log the peer has acked (`None` before its first `Hello`).

applied.description: How far of the peer's log we have applied (`None`: nothing of it yet).

behind_in.description: Rows of the peer's we have not applied, when its head is known.

behind_out.description: Rows of ours the peer has not acked (`head - acked`), once `acked` is known.

held.description: We hold our log from the peer (its agent schema is older).

held_by_peer.description: The peer holds its log from us (our agent schema is older).

last_error.description: The last failure with this peer, `"<phase>: <error>"`.

peer_head.description: The peer's log head as last seen (its `Hello`, then its rows).

schema.description: The agent schema the peer's `Hello` reported (`None`: pre-183 or no `Hello` yet).

since.description: When `up` last changed (RFC 3339); `None` before the first stream.

up.description: A stream with the peer is up now.

method.sessionsync.output.Retention.description: What happens to a root tree's data when it closes.

oneOf.description: Persisted in the durable store and data dir.
In-memory store, scratch files; nothing survives the close (51 §4).

method.sessionsync.output.SessionId.description: Identifies a conversation; every event carries one.

method.sessionsync.output.SessionOpen.description:
Reply to `create_session` / `resume_private`: the opened session, its
root, and for a private root the lease secret the owner presents on
resume and leave.

lease_secret.description:
Private roots only: the secret presented on `resume_private` and
`leave_session`; rotated on every resume.

root.description: Root of its tree (`session` itself for a fresh root).

session.description: The session that was opened or resumed.

method.sessionsync.output.SessionOrphan.description:
One undelivered stretch of a session's history on this engine (68 §4.3):
rows this engine wrote as owner in `epoch` that a later owner superseded.

at.description: When the first orphaned row was written (RFC 3339, from its HLC).

method.sessionsync.output.SessionOwner.description: `session_owner` reply and the payload of a completed `session_take`.

owner.description: Owner engine (mesh `EngineId` as text; `""` on a lone engine).

elsewhere.description: Durable sessions owned by another engine.

engine.description: This engine's mesh `EngineId` as text; `""` on a lone engine.

last_snapshot.description:

method.sessionsync.receiver.PeerSync.description:
`sessions_sync` entry: this engine's `theuth/sessions/1` session-log
replication with one peer, from memory (no store read). Seqs are log
positions: ours of our own log, the peer's of its own.

acked.description: How far of our log the peer has acked (`None` before its first `Hello`).

applied.description: How far of the peer's log we have applied (`None`: nothing of it yet).

behind_in.description: Rows of the peer's we have not applied, when its head is known.

behind_out.description: Rows of ours the peer has not acked (`head - acked`), once `acked` is known.

held.description: We hold our log from the peer (its agent schema is older).

held_by_peer.description: The peer holds its log from us (our agent schema is older).

last_error.description: The last failure with this peer, `"<phase>: <error>"`.

peer_head.description: The peer's log head as last seen (its `Hello`, then its rows).

schema.description: The agent schema the peer's `Hello` reported (`None`: pre-183 or no `Hello` yet).

since.description: When `up` last changed (RFC 3339); `None` before the first stream.

up.description: A stream with the peer is up now.

method.tasks.output.Checkout.description: The session working a task right now (67 §7.5, decision 21).

epoch.description: Bumped on every checkout, so a resumed task's stale writer loses.

orphaned.description:
Set by the orphan sweep (67 §7.5): the session is presumed lost; the
next checkout may take the task and bumps `epoch`.

progress_at_ms.description: Last progress note (ms since epoch); the orphan timer runs from here.

taken.description:
Set with `orphaned` when the sweep took the session onto `engine`
(68 §4.4): the `Resume` wake continues that session.

method.tasks.output.Kind.description:
What a reference points at. `id` is whatever the read tool for the kind
accepts: `DocId`, concept id (optionally `@<commit>`), artifact `call_id`,
`SessionId`, `MeetingId`.

oneOf.description: A knowledge concept, optionally a past revision (`id@<commit>`).

refused.description: `<title>: <why>` for each one that could not move (its agent is not there).

method.tasks.output.Owner.description:
Who owns (or reviews) a task. JSON: `{ "type": "agent", "name": "ops" }` |
`{ "type": "user" }`; text (columns, filters, prompts): `agent:ops` | `user`.

oneOf.description: The harness itself: reviewer of a schedule task its `until` closed (67 §7.4).

method.tasks.output.Priority.description:
How soon a task wants attention (132 D4). The user alone sets it; one
[`crate::rank::rank`] orders the inbox and an agent's wake dispatch by it.

oneOf.description: Its own group at the top of the rail.

accent.description:
Accent colour, a palette name from [`ACCENTS`]; `None` = no accent. Display only
(graph cards, board cards); a child without one may show its nearest ancestor's.

attachments.description:
Things attached to the task (70 TASK-ATTACHMENTS): the same references a chat
message carries (design 66) — notes, knowledge, artifacts, chats, meetings. A desk
sees them as `[attached …]` lines under the brief and reads them with the per-kind tools.

blocks.description: Tasks whose `blockers` name this one (the inverse, computed on read, never stored).

done_when.description:
Acceptance criteria (70 DESK-PROTOCOL): what `done` is judged against
first. Drafted from the brief by whoever creates the task when the user
did not state it; `None` = judged on the user's evident intention, and
then self-review is not allowed.

home.description:
182 D1: the engine (mesh id) that works the task — only it dispatches,
checks out and sweeps it; `None` = a legacy row, worked by the hub
lease holder. Stamped at creation; changed only by `task_move_home`.

next_wake_after_ms.description: Back-off: no wake is delivered before this (ms since epoch).

no_progress_count.description: Consecutive wakes that changed no field (67 §7.3 back-off).

parent.description: Delegation tree.

priority.description: How soon it wants attention (132 D4); the user alone sets it.

project.description: Project label (`agent`'s `projects.name`, the session project); `None` = no project.

resolved_blockers.description:
214 A1: task ids that were in `blockers` until that task closed (done/cancelled) —
the finished dependencies, kept for the graph. A manual removal does not add here.

reviewer.description: Who marks it done; `None` = the owner's `reports_to`.

schedule.description: Routine provenance: `(schedule name, fire time ms)`; the coalescing key (67 §7.4).

thread.description: Thread document id (59): comments, questions, answers, notes.

where.description: Engine name, written by theuth at delegation (67 §8).

method.tasks.output.TaskState.description: Where a task is in its life (67 §7.2).

oneOf.description: Created, not dispatched: no wake, no placement, not in any desk inbox.
Queued for the owner: woken, placed, in the desk inbox; not checked out.
Checked out by the owner's session.
Owner finished; waits for the reviewer.
Waiting on a decision, a person or another task.

method.tasks.receiver.AttachRef.description:
One attached reference: `title`/`meta` are frozen at attach time and are
display text only; `meta` may be empty.

id.description: The id the read tool for `kind` accepts.

meta.description: Display-only facts (`pdf v2 · 3 pages`); may be empty.

title.description: Human name as the user saw it; never empty (a missing one is filled from the id by whoever renders).

method.telegram.output.SessionId.description: Identifies a conversation; every event carries one.

method.telegram.output.TelegramEvent.description: Bus event: connection and rendering state (98 §13).

topics.description: Topics are enabled for the bot.

oneOf.description: A poll error (the loop backs off), or `hub lease held elsewhere`.
A call was still rate limited after the client's retries.
A bubble left Draft mode, or rich → plain (98 §8.3).
The chat cannot be written to; its thread was unbound (98 §4.3).
A pairing link was minted; show it as a QR (09 `LinkUrl` shape).
Terminal mode: the channel only runs in `t --headless`.

98c: the actor is up but the vault has not answered yet; `Status`
reports this instead of guessing `Unconfigured`. Never on the bus.

method.telegram.output.TelegramStatus.description: Snapshot served by [`Status`], `/telegram status`, `telegram_status` and RPC (98 §13).

dropped_updates.description: Updates ignored (unknown kinds, edits, channel posts, …).

groups.description: Chats where mentions and commands are honoured.

polling.description: This engine holds the lease and the poller is up.

state.description: Last state event; `None` before the supervisor has reported.

method.tools.output.Risk.description: How much damage a tool can do; the only input to the approval policy.

oneOf.description: Changes state that can be undone or is scoped.
Irreversible or unbounded (arbitrary shell, delete, network writes).

method.tools.output.ToolSpec.description: What the model sees for a tool.

direct.description:
Offered as a direct tool definition even when the runtime is on
(08 §0.4): the floor is the tools that talk to the user or to other
agents; everything that returns data is a runtime function only.

name.description: Unique name. MCP tools register under their remote name, no prefix (01 §1.4).

returns.description:
Python annotation of what the runtime function returns (`ToolOutput::
structured` when set, else the text): `str`, `list[dict]`, `Any`, ...

schema.description: JSON Schema for the arguments object.

method.update.output.UpdateReady.description:
Event: a newer version was verified and is on disk (`applied: true`), or
exists but the binary's directory is not writable (`applied: false`)
(39 §3.2). Published once per version.

applied.description:
`true`: the next start of `theuth` runs it. `false`: `t --update`
(with `sudo`) installs it.

method.web.input.Recency.description: Recency filter; each provider maps it to its own date syntax.

method.web.output.ProviderProbe.description: Outcome of one probe query through one provider (Settings › Search "Test").

detail.description: Error text (or the failure kind) when not ok; first hit title when ok.

rows.description: Rows it returned.

method.web.output.ProviderStatus.description: Wire form of one provider's last known state.

detail.description: Human detail: `"12 rows"` or the error text.

external.description: Registered from `search-providers` (keyed or self-hosted), not a built-in engine.

kind.description:
Failure class of the last error: `rate_limited`, `captcha`, `challenge`,
`blocked`, `parse_error`, `timeout`, `unauthorized`, `http`; empty when ok.

last_error_at.description: RFC 3339 of the last failed call.

last_ok_at.description: RFC 3339 of the last successful call.

ok.description: Last call succeeded; `None` when never called.

searches.description: Whether the provider answers searches at all (render-only ones do not).

method.web.output.SearchTestResult.description: One full `search_web` run from Settings › Search ("Run a test search").

is_error.description: The tool flagged the run as an error (all providers failed, or degraded with `degraded_is_error`).

text.description: The tool text the model would see.

method.webprofile.input.Cookie.description: One cookie with every attribute (209 D1, §4.1). `value` is a credential: `Debug` redacts it.

domain.description: Domain as the store gives it (a leading `.` is tolerated and ignored for grouping).

expires.description: Unix seconds, or `null` for a session cookie.

host_only.description: `true`: sent to `domain` only, not its subdomains (`__Host-` cookies need it).

partitioned.description: CHIPS `Partitioned`; kept although WebKit cannot carry the partition key (209 D1).

method.webprofile.input.CookieChange.description: One change of a push (209 §4.4): `{op:"set", cookie}` | `{op:"remove", name, domain, path}`.

oneOf.description: Set (replace) the cookie of this key; an `expires` in the past removes it.
Remove the cookie of this key.

method.webprofile.input.OriginStorage.description: One origin's localStorage snapshot (209 §4.1 `origins[]`, §4.4 `storage[]`). Values redacted in `Debug`.

captured_ms.description: Unix ms of the capture; a newer capture replaces an older one, an older one is ignored.

local_storage.description: `[key, value]` pairs in the page's order.

epoch.description: The profile epoch after the clear; pushes under an older one are `stale-epoch`.

site.description: The registrable domain forgotten (the asked host's eTLD+1).

method.webprofile.output.ForgottenSite.description: One forgotten site of `web_profile_pull` (209 §4.1 forget marker).

forgotten_ms.description: Unix ms of the forget (the forgetting engine's clock).

method.webprofile.output.ProfileMode.description: Config `browser.profile` (209 D6): `shared` (default) or `off` (no push, load or save; rows stay).

oneOf.description: One profile for the tile and every agent browser of the mesh.
Nothing is pushed, loaded or saved.

method.webprofile.output.ProfileStatus.description:
`web_profile_status`'s result (209 §4.4): the mode and the profile's size, cheap (no row is
opened), for Settings.

sites.description: Sites with live rows (kept also while off, until cleared).

method.webprofile.output.PullResult.description:
`web_profile_pull`'s result (209 §4.4, D5): one page of the profile's cookies and snapshots of
`sites`. Every site in `sites` is answered whole: a client sets what it gets and deletes from
its store the cookies of those sites it did not get (a forgotten site answers nothing).
`Debug` redacts every value; nothing logs it.

cookies.description: Every live cookie of those sites, sorted by site, then name, domain and path.

forgotten.description:
Every site forgotten in the last 30 days of this epoch, with when (on every page). The
client deletes from its store the cookies of each one forgotten after its previous
`basis_ms` before it applies this answer's cookies.

next.description:
More sites follow: pull again with the same `sites` and this as `cursor`. `null` when this
page is the last.

now_ms.description:
The engine's clock (Unix ms) just before it read this page: the first page's is the
client's next `basis_ms` once every page arrived.

profile.description: `"shared"`, or `"off"` when `browser.profile: off`: then no site is answered.

sites.description:
The sites this page covers, sorted: the asked ones as registrable domains, or every site
the profile holds (also one whose cookies all expired) when none were asked. A cookie of
the client's store belongs to a site when its domain (lower case, no leading `.`) is the
site or ends with `.` and the site.

storage.description: Every localStorage snapshot of those sites, sorted by site, then origin.

method.webprofile.output.PulledCookie.description:
One cookie of `web_profile_pull` (209 §4.4, D5): the [`Cookie`] fields, plus its site and
the writer and time of its row, so a client skips echoes of its own pushes (`tile:<device>`).
`Debug` redacts the value.

domain.description: Domain as the store gives it (a leading `.` is tolerated and ignored for grouping).

expires.description: Unix seconds, or `null` for a session cookie.

host_only.description: `true`: sent to `domain` only, not its subdomains (`__Host-` cookies need it).

partitioned.description: CHIPS `Partitioned`; kept although WebKit cannot carry the partition key (209 D1).

updated_ms.description: Unix ms of its row's write.

method.webprofile.output.PulledStorage.description:
One origin's localStorage snapshot of `web_profile_pull`, with its site and row writer and time.
`Debug` redacts the values.

captured_ms.description: Unix ms of the capture; a newer capture replaces an older one, an older one is ignored.

local_storage.description: `[key, value]` pairs in the page's order.

updated_ms.description: Unix ms of its row's write.

epoch.description: The profile epoch the rows were written under.

profile.description:
`"shared"`, or `"off"` when `browser.profile: off` made the push a no-op (209 D6): the
client stops pushing until it reads `"shared"` again.

refused.description:
Sites whose sets and snapshots were refused because the site was forgotten after the
push's `basis_ms` (or the push named none), sorted; its removes still applied. The client
pulls to learn the forget and does not push those sets again.

sites.description: Sites whose rows were written, sorted.

method.webprofile.output.SiteSummary.description: One entry of `web_profile_sites` (209 §4.4): counts, never values.

updated_ms.description: Unix ms of the row's last write.

epoch.description: The profile epoch after the clear; pushes under an older one are `stale-epoch`.

site.description: The registrable domain forgotten (the asked host's eTLD+1).

method.webprofile.receiver.ForgottenSite.description: One forgotten site of `web_profile_pull` (209 §4.1 forget marker).

forgotten_ms.description: Unix ms of the forget (the forgetting engine's clock).
